subject: Weekly leadership checkpoint — QBR readiness + OKR pivots
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: leadership@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly leadership checkpoint — QBR readiness + OKR pivots

Hello leadership team —

Quick, data-driven update for this week as we lock the QBR package and decide a small set of OKR pivots. TL;DR: product stability + cost-per-token trajectory are the focus; three asks at the bottom.

Wins
- Hosted API latency profile: p95 down 12% week-over-week after kernel tuning (see attached QBR_one_pager.pdf).
- Redwood Dedicated pilot: baseline throughput targets met in internal stress test (3 clients, sustained 2k rps).
- Eval harness flagged no regressions on high-precision prompts across latest model build.

Risks / Constraints
- Dedicated procurement timeline: vendor SLA addendum pending legal sign-off — this creates a 2–3 week execution risk for customer pilots.
- Customer-facing regression exposed on long-chat context (>=8k tokens) for one enterprise tenant — mitigation deployed but we need a permanence roadmap.
- Cost trend for high-concurrency workloads has a potential overspend vs forecast if batching parameters are not tuned before QBR.

Asks (decisions / owners)
1) Approve temporary OKR pivot: shift "Model Serving Latency" from 2-week sprint target to a performance stabilization lane through the next QBR to prioritize reliability work. (Decision needed by EOD Tue, 17 Aug). — owner: soojin_lee
2) Authorize procurement exception to enable expedited Dedicated capacity validation (one-time spend up to $45k). Impact: removes the vendor procurement blocker for pilot customers. (Approve or route to finance by 18 Aug). — owner: jonas_weber
3) Exec review slot: 20-minute sync during Tuesday leadership block to sign off on the QBR one-pager and approve the above asks. Please confirm attendance. — owner: laura_bennett

Attachments: QBR_one_pager.pdf, OKR_progress_sheet.xlsx, Dedicated_capacity_runbook.md

Notes: I included a one-page QBR summary and an OKR progress sheet with proposed minor target adjustments highlighted in yellow. If we approve the procurement exception, Jonas will coordinate with Finance and Legal to expedite signatures.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, leadership@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership checkpoint — QBR readiness + OKR pivots

Thanks for the crisp status, Soojin — this is helpful. A couple quick asks from my side:

- For Ask #1 (OKR pivot): can you call out the specific metric(s) we would deprioritize and a short impact sentence I can include in the QBR notes?
- For Ask #2 (procurement exception): if we approve the spend, what are the exact contract terms we will accept (term, data residency, SLA)? I want Finance to have the list when we route.

I'll block the 20-minute slot on Tuesday; expect me there.

Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, leadership@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership checkpoint — QBR readiness + OKR pivots

On Sun, Aug 15, 2027 at 09:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Wins
> - Hosted API latency profile: p95 down 12% week-over-week after kernel tuning (see attached QBR_one_pager.pdf).

Appreciate the summary. Quick clarifications and next steps from procurement/ops side:

- For the OKR pivot: proposed change is to shift target dates rather than drop the metric. Recommend we say: "Stabilize p95 latency at <= current baseline; shift aggressive reduction target to Q3 close-out" — that gives the QBR narrative and keeps the team focused on reliability.
- Contract terms for the procurement exception: short list we can sign off on to expedite: 12-month term, standard Redwood DPA + SOC 2 attestation, cancellation with 30-day notice for trial customers, and a capped liability clause per vendor standard. If Legal flags anything, we'll call it out in the Tuesday sync.

I will take ownership of Ask #2 — will get Finance and Legal the vendor addendum and a one-page summary for approval today. Also will coordinate a small runbook update (Dedicated_capacity_runbook.md) for the pilots so CS can onboard customers quickly if approved.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Gomez <maria@acmedigital.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, leadership@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership checkpoint — QBR readiness + OKR pivots

Thanks for the update, Soojin — and thanks Jonas for taking point on procurement. From Acme's side: we want to keep our pilot timeline but can be flexible on a 2-week extension if it helps stabilization. I'll update our mutual action plan and share an amended timeline by EOD Wednesday.

Also attaching the specific long-chat logs that showed the regression (attachment stub: acme_longchat_sample.txt) — feel free to ping me if you want raw traces.

Best,
Maria Gomez
Head of AI Integrations
Acme Digital
